title: EpiWorld: Grounding LLM Policy Agents in Epidemiological World Models

claim.summary: EpiWorld grounds an LLM policy actor in a graph-structured, action-conditioned epidemiological world model and a tiered skill library of protocol constraints, surveillance estimators and after-action lessons, using counterfactual rollouts to evaluate and refine weekly regional intervention policies.

modules.name: Action-conditioned epidemic world-model rollout
modules.scope_reason: Interventions enter as per-region FiLM modulation of the latent state and rollouts score candidate policies by projected hospitalisation burden, so the action interface and feedback signal are tied to the epidemic-intervention output rather than reusable across task families.
evidence_locators: PDF p.2; passage beginning "Candidate policies are then evaluated through"
PDF p.3; passage beginning "We propose an epidemiological world model"

modules.name: Protocol-constrained tiered epidemiological skill library
modules.scope_reason: Protocol predicates fix an admissible intervention envelope and surveillance estimators (Rt, severity ratios, stringency index) condition the proposed action, so the state and action space are defined by the epidemic-policy output.
evidence_locators: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Protocol Constraints are deterministic procedures"
PDF p.6; passage beginning "Adaptive Lessons can refine Surveillance Skill"

modules.name: After-action lesson distillation with supersession
modules.scope_reason: The insert-and-supersede bank update is generic, but each lesson is a confidence-weighted adjustment to surveillance-skill parameters indexed by behavioural and regional tags and distilled from intervention failures such as capacity-limit violations, so the lesson content is bound to the epidemic decision task.
evidence_locators: PDF p.6; passage beginning "a teacher module performs retrospective analysis"
